second_order: bringing joke material back from Discord
theme_note: One participant carries supplied April Fools text from Discord into a subreddit performance; later venue-moving codes can extend this if they do the same practical work.

second_order: trying out and reacting to changed flairs
theme_note: Members notice, praise, wait for, and later negotiate the April Fools replacements attached to their accounts.

second_order: posting fake releases and remaking familiar formats
theme_note: Posters turn release, throwback, discussion, jukebox, and related familiar forms into April Fools performances.

second_order: falling for, exposing, and judging the gags
theme_note: Commenters recognize the date, admit being fooled, question sincerity, complain, defend repetitions, or award winners, making the fake-outs legible in uptake.

second_order: planning and chaining one-word lyric posts
theme_note: Members turn isolated words and symbols into a planned, serial lyric performance across threads.

second_order: flooding the room with memes and one-line shitposts
theme_note: Short meme prompts, emoji, provocations, petitions, and self-descriptions make participation itself the shared April Fools performance, apart from fake release/news formats.

second_order: taking the shitposting to the plug
theme_note: A participant invites the room into its off-platform listening venue; later codes can extend this when people explicitly move the activity there.

second_order: calling people to join Team Purple through a fake pop claim
theme_note: This single ambiguous call combines the local fake-release form with colour-team recruitment but supplies no target, coordinates, or uptake tying it to the canvas.

second_order: calling for and answering a collective r/place saxophone
theme_note: A public canvas petition asks the room to draw a saxophone and receives a colour-team reply, without yet showing coordinates or placement.

second_order: aiming local jokes at named outside audiences
theme_note: A fake collaboration is explicitly addressed to Australians and an outside subreddit is tagged as an audience, without showing reciprocal coordination.

second_order: proposing canvas designs and moving decisions to Discord
theme_note: Public calls, drafts, site suggestions, and feasibility talk hold together as attempts to turn interest into a shared canvas object; what varies is the proposed object and whether the choice remains public or moves to Discord.

second_order: ending the joke and deciding what to keep
theme_note: These codes close and assess the subreddit event: people ask when it ends, moderators restore ordinary posting, and the town hall weighs its delay, rankings, and residue. What varies is whether the act is closure, retrospective judgment, or retention.

second_order: building and reporting progress on the RAWM saxophone
theme_note: Instructions, joining, completion reports, help, and assessments hold together as the visible work of making the chosen saxophone. What varies is whether participants direct pixels, contribute, or report how the result looks.

second_order: keeping the sax first when other canvas ideas appear
theme_note: Expansion, labeling, and a parallel Sia-wig proposal are handled by putting the small shared sax first or testing additions against available space and people. What varies is whether the alternative is lettering, a larger image, new territory, or another pop reference.

second_order: reporting destruction and declining to rebuild
theme_note: The two reports hold together as reactions to damage: an early deletion prompts a replacement link, while the later raid is treated as final because participation is too low.
This single code frames participation as entering a warzone and does not belong with the material building, scope negotiation, or damage-response practices.

second_order: clarifying that a moderator request was about r/unawaywithme
theme_note: This single clarification prevents an unrelated subreddit invitation from being read as part of the Popheads canvas project.
This single late call proposes a starting pixel and borrowed font for the community name; with no reply or outcome, it does not join the earlier sax-building practice.
